answer: Bond every agent identity to staked collateral: a newcomer must be vouched for by established peers who risk slashing if it misbehaves. Picture the trust graph as a living atlas where each node earns its coordinates. A liar fades from bright ember to dull umber as its stake burns, warning the network. Minting a thousand sybils then costs a thousand real bonds, so fake swarms stay too expensive to sustain.
